cells.rule: K3.1: "store into an `owned` field or owning-collection slot, including through a `set(owned)` accessor" | §28.6: "A **freshly-produced owned value** — a `new` expression, a call returning `owned T`, a `move` expression, or an owned operator result — stored into a non-`owned` (borrow) field is an **error**" | K3.13: "An **unmarked read of a class-typed binding never consumes**" | §28.3: "An indexer assignment of such a value is not reached by this bullet: it is a call of the indexer's setter, or a"
cells.cite: §28.3 (K3.1, K3.13, field-store bullet cl.2–3, property-store bullet), §28.5, §28.6, §28.7, App. C.3
cells.note: Into an `owned` field, or through `set(owned)`: a marker-free consume. The new holder disposes it on overwrite or teardown. Into a non-`owned` field or property: a fresh or `move`d value is rejected. An unmarked owned binding is a borrow of a scope-bound binding, so clause 2 rejects it. Through a user-declared indexer setter, a fresh temporary or scope-bound borrow is admitted at the call under clause 3's residual (it dangles past its boundary; the K4.1 backstop catches the use). This is an explicit, recorded asymmetry with property stores. Re-walked at v0.331: no v0.331 edit touches the field-store bullet, K3.1, §28.6 or the property-store bullet's instance half; #5681 widens K3.2 only for an async return.

cells.rule: §28.3 field-store cl.2: "borrows sourced from a parameter that is **not `owned`** — a plain or `scoped` parameter — or from the receiver are admissible; scope-bound locals and temporaries are rejected" | cl.3: "whether the caller-side source actually outlives the object is the programmer's obligation, not a compile-time guarantee" | K4.3: "A borrow held inside an object a static references is that object's field-, collection- or frame-held clause"
cells.cite: §28.3 (field-store bullet cl.1–5, property-store bullet), §28.6, §28.14, K2.3, K4.3, App. C.3, K4.3 (static-held sentence, v0.331)
cells.note: Bounded by the structural check plus the K4.3-recorded residual: the caller-side source must outlive the object, with the K4.1 backstop live in checked mode and the domain clause recorded. A `scoped` class- or interface-typed parameter makes the bound static. A scope-bound local, an `owned` parameter or a temporary is rejected at a direct or property store. Through a plain parameter the callee stores (a user indexer setter included), it is admitted at the call under clause 3. v0.331 (0151) adds one decided sub-case: a parameter borrow stored into a field of an object a static references stays this field-held residual, with §22.12 rule 4's confinement obligation where the static is warned. #5680 restates that a slot-current-value borrow keeps K5.6's flag posture; no verdict moves.

cells.rule: §9.7: "A borrow-bearing record value may not be stored in an **instance field of a class**" | "The checked-mode trust regime is therefore unavailable and the store is **rejected statically**" | "Stores of the **null-source** form are admitted"
cells.cite: §9.7 (instance-field bullet, null-source definition), §28.3 property-store bullet, §8.6, App. C.3
cells.note: Rejected statically, with no residual, except for the null-source form (every reference-typed component null). Property stores are judged as the same field store, and a user-indexer setter body storing `value` hits the same bullet. Boxing to an `Object` or interface field is a borrow-erasing rejection. A generic `Keep<Pair>` is rejected per instantiation. Re-hunted at v0.331: a `ref _p` location over a Pair-typed field is judged "exactly as the direct assignment" (§28.3 ref/out rule), so the same bullet rejects. A fresh owned collection that carries Pair borrows (`_keep := xs.ToArray()`) is the #5693 route, recorded in the R3–R6 × C3 stdlib-copy cell.

cells.rule: §15.1.2: "When such an array is passed by value, returned from a method, stored as a field, or captured by a closure, the same borrow-lifetime rules apply that govern borrow-bearing records" | §15.1.2 slot store: "is checked as an assignment to the array's holder" | §28.3 property-store bullet: "and a borrow-bearing record or choice value is admitted only in the null-source form"
cells.cite: §15.1.2, §3.6 (holds-borrows row), §9.7 (instance-field bullet), §28.3 (field-store and property-store bullets); DECLINED.md (async inline-array row)
cells.note: Rejected statically outside the null-source form (every slot null), for `[N]Pair` and for `[N]C` alike: §3.6 keys §9.7 on holds-borrows, and the property-store bullet's lead sentence routes a borrow-bearing inline array to §9.7's instance-field bullet. The v0.330 cross-check (X1, DECIDED-BY) settled the two readings for (A). v0.331 left the property-store verdict sentence ("a borrow-bearing record or choice value is admitted only in the null-source form") still without "inline array", a drafting gap and not a second rule. The verdict field moves from conditional to rejected to match that decision; the status does not change.

cells.rule: §35.4: "may not be stored in a class instance field or (outside the null-source form) a static field" | §15.3: "may not be a class field, since a class instance's lifetime is not bounded by any borrow source's scope"
cells.cite: §35.4 (holds-borrows), §9.7 (instance-field bullet, read 'record or choice'), §15.3 (field placement), §28.3 property-store bullet, App. C.3
cells.note: Rejected statically except in the null-source form (a payload-free case, or every payload reference null). An owning choice that holds borrows cannot be a class field at all.

cells.rule: §9.7: "so no span is storable in a static field or in a class instance field at all" | stdlib §4.16: "A buffer- or array-backed span is therefore never storable in a static field or in a class instance field" | stdlib §4.14: "it can be stored anywhere the borrow's lifetime allows, including as a class field when the field's enclosing class outlives the borrow source"
cells.cite: §9.7 (instance-field bullet; static-field bullet's span sentence), stdlib §4.16 (Boxing and lifetime), stdlib §4.14 (Why not stack-allocated like C#'s Span<T>?); #5692
cells.note: Spec §9.7 and stdlib §4.16 reject every span store into a class instance field (no span has a null-source value). Stdlib §4.14's Q&A paragraph, which is normative stdlib text, admits one "when the field's enclosing class outlives the borrow source". The paragraph predates v0.331, and the v0.330 cell missed it. Filed as #5692 (OPEN, spec-defect). The intended verdict is not in doubt: rejected, since rationale §5.15 withdrew the gloss at v0.180. The fix is doc-only.

cells.rule: §28.3 Set-erasing positions: "the `as` itself is the set-erasing position, judged at the conversion whatever then holds its result" | sink rule: "While its source set is non-empty, a function value may not be stored in a field, in any collection, in a property or indexer" | App. C.3: "carries the sources of the borrows that value holds in its source set, so it meets the sink rule as any capture-bearing closure does"
cells.cite: §28.3 (closure bullet: sink rule, provenance clauses 1, 2 and 5; Function-typed holders cl.1–3; Set-erasing positions), §9.7 (capture bullet), App. C.3; #5675, proposal 0148
cells.note: A non-empty-set function value is rejected at every instance-field route. A function-typed field, property or indexer, record component, choice payload and inline-array slot are holders under the sink rule. A field declared `Object` or at a bare type parameter is set-erasing. An explicit `f as Object` (#5675) is now itself the set-erasing position, rejected at the conversion, so `_o := f as Object` no longer escapes. Since 0148, a closure over a span, a borrow-bearing record or a method reference bound to such a receiver carries a non-empty set, so it can no longer reach a function-typed field as empty-set (an escape that was live at v0.330). The only storage is a `scoped` field (C13). Hunted with `f is Object o` (a pattern binding is in the implicit-conversion list), `new Box(f)` at `record Box(O: Object)`, `b.V := f` at `Box<() -> int>`, and a capture-bearing closure nested in an outer one: each is rejected.

cells.rule: §9.7: "and is rejected wherever `Keep<Pair>` is named, by the instance-field bullet, the diagnostic naming the store" | §28.3: "A field declared at a bare type parameter is reached from outside the generic body only through a receiver whose instantiation substitutes a function type for it" | §28.5: "the restriction "only fields of class or interface types may be `owned`" is checked at *instantiation*"
cells.cite: §28.1 (class-or-interface assumption), §28.3 (field-store bullet cl.2, set-erasing positions), §9.7 (generic-body paragraph), §28.5 (generic class fields), §3.6 rule 2
cells.note: The body is checked under the class-or-interface assumption: the field-store residual for a parameter or receiver source, rejection for scope-bound sources, and K3.1 for `owned T` fields. Re-checked per instantiation: a substitution that holds borrows is rejected wherever named. A function substitution is a set-erasing field (the caller checks capture-freedom), and an inadmissible `owned` substitution is an instantiation-site error. v0.331: inside the generic body, an `as` or typed pattern at the body's own type parameter is now a set-erasing position at the declaration (#5675, T1 critique B3), which closes `_v := f as T` into a bare-T field. A captured T counts per instantiation (0148). No verdict moves.

cells.rule: K1.6: "Values of runtime-managed type (`string`, `Type`, boxed value types, function values) and of ordinary value type carry no classification and no obligation" | §9.7: "runtime-managed values have unbounded lifetime by construction"
cells.note: No borrow, unrestricted. A boxed primitive in an `Object` or interface field is a runtime-managed value. `owned` on `string`/`Type`/function fields is rejected (§28.5), which is irrelevant to borrows.

cells.rule: §22.12 r2: "assigning a fresh owned value into an admitted mutable static discharges the producer" | §22.13: "Static `owned` fields are disposed at program exit" | §28.3: "a borrowed local may not be assigned to any field" | K9.4: "static owned fields admit no `move`" | §28.3 Static stores: "a freshly-produced owned value (a `new` expression, a call returning `owned T`, a `move` expression, an owned operator result) is discharged and made process-lived wherever"
cells.cite: §22.12 rule 2 (forms i, ii, iv; Store semantics), §22.13 (static class-typed fields without `owned`), §28.3 (K3.1, K9.4, field-store bullet cl.1, property-store bullet), App. C.3, §28.3 Static stores (v0.331)
cells.note: A `static owned` (readonly) field takes the value under K3.1 and disposes it at program exit. A non-`owned` `static readonly` field, or an admitted mutable static (form i or ii only; other class or interface types are errors at the declaration), discharges a fresh or `move`d producer, and the referent is process-lived. An overwrite never disposes. An unmarked owned local is a borrow of a scope-bound binding and is rejected. No borrow arises, so nothing outlives a source. v0.331 (0151) restates this unchanged in the new Static stores bullet, whose remedy list names `_m := move m;`. An unmarked owned local is "a local in any state" and is rejected there.

cells.rule: §28.3 Static stores: "admits it only when it is static-storage-sourced" | "A borrow of any other source — a plain or `scoped` parameter, `this`, a field, getter or indexer reached through the receiver, a capture, a local in any state, an `owned` parameter, a temporary, or the result of invoking a function value — is a compile error at the store." | K4.3: "No clause covers a static-held borrow, and none is needed"
cells.cite: §28.3 (Static stores of a class- or interface-typed value; property-store bullet, static half), §22.12 rule 2 (v0.331 sentence), K4.3, App. C.3; §22.3 (ref targets); proposal 0151, #5676
cells.note: Admitted only when static-storage-sourced: a bare read of a `static` field or of `T.P`. Every admissible static form keeps its referents alive to process exit, so the bound is K2's always-live source. A borrow reached through a static (`T.f.g`, `T.P.Peek()`) is not static storage. Every other borrow is rejected at the store, so the v0.330 counterexample (`_m := m;` from a plain parameter) is now an error. Hunted routes: (1) `ref` into a static. A mutable static field or auto-property is not a `ref` target (§22.3). A block-form static property is copy-in/copy-out, and its write-back is judged "exactly as the direct assignment", which is the static-property store and so rejected. (2) A block-form static setter storing `value`: a plain parameter, rejected. (3) A lambda storing a capture: rejected. (4) A borrow into a field or collection of an object a static holds: K4.3's field- or collection-held clause with rule 4's confinement (R2/C1, R2/C3). Locked<T> rejects a borrowing interior (§30.12). None escapes.

cells.rule: §9.7: "A borrow-bearing record may not be stored in a static field of any type, *except* when every reference-typed field (and every reference-typed slot of every inline-array field) of the value is `null`"
cells.cite: §9.7 (static-field bullet), §22.12 rule 4(f) and table row 'holds borrows', App. C.3
cells.note: Only the null-source form. A mutable static of such a type is an (iii)-closed error at the declaration, and `static readonly` admits only null-source values, so no borrow reaches static storage.

cells.rule: App. C.3: "may be stored in a static field only when every reference-typed field or payload (and every reference-typed slot of every inline-array field) of the value, through nested record and choice components, is null"
cells.cite: §22.12 rule 4(f) and table row 'holds borrows', §9.7 (static-field bullet), §15.1.2, App. C.3
cells.note: A plain inline array carrying borrows is named by §22.12 note (f) and goes to §9.7's static bullet: null-source only (every slot null). A mutable static is an (iii)-closed error.

cells.rule: §35.4: "may not be stored in a class instance field or (outside the null-source form) a static field" | §22.12 4(g): "is a **compile error at the declaration site** naming this rule, whether or not it also holds borrows"
cells.cite: §9.7 (static-field bullet), §22.12 rule 4(f)/(g), §35.4, App. C.3
cells.note: Non-owning choice: null-source only (f). Owning-classified choice: rejected at the declaration (g). A mutable static is an (iii)-closed error.

cells.rule: §9.7: "so no span is storable in a static field or in a class instance field at all" | stdlib §4.16: "A buffer- or array-backed span is therefore never storable in a static field or in a class instance field" | stdlib §4.14: "it can be stored anywhere the borrow's lifetime allows"
cells.cite: §9.7 (static-field bullet), §22.12 rule 4(f), stdlib §4.16; stdlib §4.14 (Why not stack-allocated); #5692
cells.note: Rejected: no span has a null-source value. `ReadOnlyStringSpan` falls under §22.12's record-without-borrows row. Stdlib §4.14's general clause "anywhere the borrow's lifetime allows" could be read to admit a span over static storage into a static. But its only named instance is a class field (R6/C1), and §9.7 and stdlib §4.16 name statics explicitly, so no passage gives this cell a contrary verdict. #5692's fix (replace the clause with "locals, parameters and components of other borrow-bearing values") should cover statics in the same edit.

cells.rule: §28.3: "While its source set is non-empty, a function value may **not** be stored in a field, in any collection, in a property or indexer" | §22.12 4(e): "**Function type:** a function-typed static warns" | §28.3 Set-erasing positions: "the `as` itself is the set-erasing position, judged at the conversion whatever then holds its result"
cells.cite: §28.3 (sink rule; set-erasing positions for `Object`/bare-T statics), §22.12 rule 2 table and 4(e), App. C.3; #5675, proposal 0148
cells.note: A mutable function-typed static is an error (†). A `static readonly` one warns, and in static init the sink rule rejects any non-empty set. An empty-set closure that captures value-typed locals (a mutable cell) is admitted with the 4(e) warning, which is a domain hazard, not a borrow. No `scoped` route reaches static storage. v0.331: `Gate._o := f as Object` is rejected at the `as` (#5675); 0151 is not needed for it. A closure over a span or a borrow-bearing record now has a non-empty set (0148), so it is rejected in static init too.

cells.rule: §22.12 (v): "is admitted by no form above and is a **compile error at the declaration site**, whatever the parameter's constraints or eventual substitutions" | §22.12 (i): "is admitted at the declaration and classified **per instantiation, after substitution**"
cells.cite: §22.12 rule 2 (v), rule 4 (i), §9.7 (static-field bullet), §3.6 rule 2
cells.note: A mutable `T` static is an error at the declaration. `static readonly T` is classified per instantiation: a substitution that holds borrows is null-source only, an owning choice is rejected (g), and class or interface substitutions warn. Stores happen only in static init, where scope-bound sources are rejected under the class assumption. v0.331: a class-assumed `T` store in static init is also governed by the Static stores bullet. Static init has no parameter or receiver source, so it adds no rejection a program can reach.

cells.rule: §22.12 r3: "`static readonly` of **immutable content** — value types of sendable-value category, `string`, enums — and `const`" | §22.12 r2: "a mutable static admitted by none of (i)–(iv) is a compile error naming this rule"
cells.cite: §22.12 rules 2–4 (table rows `string`, `Type`, 'any other class type'), K1.6
cells.note: No borrow arises. Reachability is limited by the sharing rules, not lifetime: a mutable `string`/`Type` static is an error, `static readonly`/`const` `string` and `static readonly Type` are unrestricted, and a boxed value in a `static readonly Object` takes rule 4's class-type warning.

cells.rule: §28.11 slot policy (owned slots): "takes `owned`; indexer-set disposes the previous value first" | §28.11: "is not a borrow of any named source but a temporary that dies at its K8 boundary" | App. C.3: "A fresh-producer element of non-trivial-dispose class type in a borrowing-family collection literal is rejected"
cells.cite: §28.11 (element slot policy, Borrowing collections, Owning collections), §15.4, K3.1, App. C.3
cells.note: Owning-family slot (Add/Insert/indexer-set/literal element/GetOrAdd factory result): an `owned` ingress, `move x` for a named binding, drop-on-overwrite at indexer-set. Borrowing-family slot: a fresh temporary passed to Add/Insert/indexer-set is admitted with §15.4's mandatory fresh-store warning; it dangles at its K8 boundary and the checked-mode backstop catches it. A non-trivial fresh literal element is rejected. An unmarked owned binding is a borrow (R2 C3).

cells.rule: §28.11: "parameter-sourced (a parameter that is not `owned`), receiver-sourced, and field-sourced borrows are admitted" | §28.11: "stored into a collection that provably outlives that scope — the collection is a field, is reachable from one, escapes the method, or is a local of strictly wider scope — is **rejected** at the store site" | slot policy (owned slots): "takes `owned`; indexer-set disposes the previous value first"
cells.cite: §28.11 (Storing a borrow; element slot policy), K2.3, K4.3, §28.3 cl.4 (domain clause)
cells.note: Borrowing slot: parameter-, receiver- and field-sourced borrows are admitted under the K4.3 residual and domain clause, with the K4.1 backstop. A scope-bound borrow into a collection that outlives its scope is rejected. Owning slot: a borrow cannot reach an `owned` ingress. A caller-supplied (parameter) collection is not in the dash list, but 'provably outlives that scope' decides it as rejected. The implementation agrees (collection_store_escape_1539.parameter_collection_rejected). v0.331: a parameter borrow added to a borrowing collection that a static holds (a warned `static readonly Array<Item>`) is the collection-held clause with §22.12 rule 4's confinement obligation (K4.3's new static-held sentence). It is not a static store.

cells.rule: §9.7: "A borrow-bearing record value may be **copied into a collection** only when every carried borrow's source provably outlives the collection's own binding scope" | "there is **no trust residual for record-carried borrows**"
cells.cite: §9.7 (collection bullet), §28.11 slot policy (copy slots)
cells.note: Admitted only when every carried source provably outlives the collection's own binding scope. A field-held, field-reachable, escaping or caller-supplied collection is rejected, with no residual. The parameter-held collection reading is settled as rejected by K2.3 + K4.3 (the v0.330 X1 cross-check: "a collection the method did not create" is still unstated in §9.7 at v0.331, but no admission exists without a recorded clause). Two routes the v0.330 cell did not see are split into their own cells: the stdlib value-copy members (R3–R6 × C3, #5693), and, for span-carried borrows, a kill of an element's source under a local collection (R6 × C3 route, #5691).

cells.rule: §15.1.2: "When such an array is passed by value, returned from a method, stored as a field, or captured by a closure, the same borrow-lifetime rules apply that govern borrow-bearing records" | §9.7: "there is **no trust residual for record-carried borrows**" | §28.11 slot policy (borrow slots): "stores the borrow; the element's source must outlive the collection's use of it"
cells.cite: §15.1.2, §3.6, §9.7 (collection bullet), §28.11 (element slot policy, copy slots)
cells.note: Read through §3.6's holds-borrows keying as R3/C3 (the v0.330 X1 cross-check: §28.11's copy-slot cell adds no residual for `[N]C`). Admitted only into a local collection whose binding scope every slot source outlives. The parameter-held collection reading is settled as rejected by K2.3 + K4.3 (the v0.330 X1 cross-check: "a collection the method did not create" is still unstated in §9.7 at v0.331, but no admission exists without a recorded clause). Two routes the v0.330 cell did not see are split into their own cells: the stdlib value-copy members (R3–R6 × C3, #5693), and, for span-carried borrows, a kill of an element's source under a local collection (R6 × C3 route, #5691).

cells.rule: §35.4: "is constrained in returns, closures, and collection copies" | §9.7: "A borrow-bearing record value may be **copied into a collection** only when every carried borrow's source provably outlives the collection's own binding scope"
cells.cite: §9.7 (collection bullet, read 'record or choice'), §35.4, §28.11 slot policy (move-only element rejected at instantiation)
cells.note: A non-owning choice that holds borrows takes §9.7's collection bullet (with "record" read as "record or choice"). An owning choice is a move-only element, rejected at instantiation for both families. The parameter-held collection reading is settled as rejected by K2.3 + K4.3 (the v0.330 X1 cross-check: "a collection the method did not create" is still unstated in §9.7 at v0.331, but no admission exists without a recorded clause). Two routes the v0.330 cell did not see are split into their own cells: the stdlib value-copy members (R3–R6 × C3, #5693), and, for span-carried borrows, a kill of an element's source under a local collection (R6 × C3 route, #5691).

cells.rule: §9.7: "A borrow-bearing record value may be **copied into a collection** only when every carried borrow's source provably outlives the collection's own binding scope" | "there is **no trust residual for record-carried borrows**"
cells.cite: §9.7 (collection bullet; IReadOnlySpan reading), §28.11 slot policy, stdlib §4.16
cells.note: Spans take §9.7's collection bullet (an `IReadOnlySpan<T>` element is read as the span; any other interface or `Object` element is a borrow-erasing rejection). Admitted only into a local collection whose binding scope the span's source outlives. The parameter-held collection reading is settled as rejected by K2.3 + K4.3 (the v0.330 X1 cross-check: "a collection the method did not create" is still unstated in §9.7 at v0.331, but no admission exists without a recorded clause). Two routes the v0.330 cell did not see are split into their own cells: the stdlib value-copy members (R3–R6 × C3, #5693), and, for span-carried borrows, a kill of an element's source under a local collection (R6 × C3 route, #5691). This cell decides the store site. The bound after the store fails for a local collection (route cell below), so the local half of R6/C3 is open through that route cell.

cells.rule: Function-typed holders: "and any collection slot. At every function-typed holder the closure bullet's sink rule holds" | Set-erasing positions: "the `as` itself is the set-erasing position, judged at the conversion whatever then holds its result"
cells.cite: §28.3 (Function-typed holders; Set-erasing positions incl. the return-slot arm; closure bullet provenance clauses 1, 2 and 5), §28.11, §9.7 (capture bullet); #5675, proposal 0148
cells.note: Every collection slot is a function-typed holder whatever its element type: `Add`, `Insert`, indexer-set, collection-literal element, `GetOrAdd`. An `Object` element slot is set-erasing too, and `objs.Add(f as Object)` is now rejected at the `as` (#5675). Since 0148, a closure over a span or a borrow-bearing record has a non-empty set. Hunted: a local function-typed inline array (a holder, §28.3 Function-typed holders cl.3), and `xs.Select(x => lambda() => s[x]).ToArray()` (the selector's TResult return slot is the return-slot arm, rejected at the call). A stdlib copy member cannot carry a capture-bearing value, because no collection can hold one. None escapes.

cells.rule: §9.7: "copies `t` into a field-held `Array<T>` is admitted at the declaration and at `Bag<Item>`" | "and rejected wherever `Bag<Pair>` is named"
cells.cite: §9.7 (collection bullet, generic-body paragraph), §28.11 (store rule), §28.3 (set-erasing positions), §14.4
cells.note: At a class substitution: the §28.11 residual. At a substitution that holds borrows: §9.7's no-residual rejection. At a function substitution: the generic method's `T` parameter is a set-erasing position, checked at the caller. Owning collections need `where T: class`. A parameter-held collection at a borrow-holding substitution inherits R3 C3's ambiguity; it is not repeated here.

cells.rule: §28.11 slot policy (shared-reference slots): "| stores the reference |" | K1.6: "Values of runtime-managed type (`string`, `Type`, boxed value types, function values) and of ordinary value type carry no classification and no obligation"
cells.cite: §28.11 (element slot policy), K1.6, §28.9
cells.note: Shared-reference slots, with no lifetime obligation. A boxed primitive in an `Object` slot carries no classification. Owning families reject runtime-managed element types at instantiation.

cells.rule: "The **ownership state of the source expression carries through unchanged**: upcasting an owned value yields an owned value of the wider type (the usual transfer rules apply at the receiving position, [§28.8](#sec-ownership-transfer))" | "a reference conversion never transfers, discharges, or creates a disposal obligation"
cells.cite: §5.1 (reference conversions), §28.1 (owned admits any class other than Type or an interface), §28.3 Producers / borrowing positions
cells.note: Unchanged at v0.331. A class value is not boxed; the upcast keeps the value owned and the receiving position's transfer rules apply. No borrow is created. Re-hunted against 0151: an owned value upcast into a static is the static-store bullet's fresh-value operand, discharged and process-lived, C2's cell, not a conversion question.

cells.rule: "upcasting a borrow yields a borrow with the same source" | "Borrowed (source: same as `x`'s source if `x` is borrowed; `x` itself if `x` is owned). The cast does not move from `x`"

A span stored in, or an iterator frame over a span stored in, a method-local collection passes the scope comparison, but a collection local is not a K5.5/K5.9 holder, so the element's source can be moved or disposed under it, and the span read has no flag. groups.statement: Captured binding reassigned after the closure is formed (or assigned inside a lambda body): the closure's source set is computed at formation and misses the later, shorter-lived source.
A bare-type-parameter position at an Object substitution is not set-erasing, so a capturing closure is stored through Keep<Object> or Box<Object> and read back capture-free.
A synchronous lambda capturing a span, passed to an async callee: the task local is untraced, so the span's source can be disposed while the task is live.
Async lambdas: a captured enclosing value that holds borrows read after the lambda's own await (#5687), and a captured token's source (#5690).
Which §30.5 row covers Task<T> or OwningTask<T> at an interface T or Object.
Stdlib §4.14 says a span can be stored in a class field when the class outlives the source; §9.7 and stdlib §4.16 say never.
A span over a field's current value, then the field slot is overwritten or reset: fields are never frozen and span reads check no flag.
